name: City of Ten Thousand Buddhas
aka: Sagely City of Ten Thousand Buddhas
tradition: Chinese Mahayana Buddhism (Chan and Pure Land)
about: The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a large Chinese Mahayana Buddhist monastery and community founded by the Venerable Master Hsuan Hua and run by the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, set on a former hospital campus in Talmage, near Ukiah in Mendocino County. Practice blends the Chan (Chinese Zen) meditation and Pure Land buddha-recitation traditions, alongside sutra study, bowing, and daily ceremonies in the monastic Buddha Halls. Lay visitors can join week-long Dharma Sessions, such as Chan meditation sessions and buddha- or bodhisattva-recitation sessions, staying overnight in simple dormitories and eating in the communal dining hall. Life on campus follows monastic norms: men and women are separated, all food is pure (vegan) vegetarian, and residents rise early and keep a quiet, disciplined schedule. Casual overnight tourism is not offered; lodging is reserved for registered session participants, special events, and volunteers.
technique: Chan (seated Zen meditation) combined with Pure Land buddha- and bodhisattva-recitation, plus bowing, sutra recitation, and study.
teacherAccess: Practice is led by the resident Dharma Realm Buddhist Association Sangha (monks and nuns); the founder, Master Hsuan Hua, passed in 1995.
retreatOptions: Week-long residential Dharma Sessions (Chan meditation sessions and recitation sessions) plus longer volunteer stays; day visits also welcome.
schedule: Sessions run roughly Saturday to Saturday within the monastic daily schedule of early-morning ceremonies, meditation, recitation, meals, and lights-out by 10:30 PM.
cost: Full-session room and board is about $200 per week ($150 for seniors and students); day visits are free.

pricePerDay.notes: Session room and board is $200/week ($150/week seniors and students); per-night figures are the weekly rate divided by 7 nights. Extra days before/after are pro-rated.

foodNotes: All food is pure Mahayana vegetarian (no meat, seafood, eggs, or pungent roots), and vegan for those who choose; meals are taken in the communal dining hall.
workNotes: Full-paying session participants (except the elderly or frail) contribute seven hours per week of community service assigned by the Guest Prefect team.
